 SUBJECT:  REQUEST TO CHANGE THE FORMAT OF THE MINUTES

BACKGROUND

Staff prepare minutes for all City Council and City advisory body meetings, including Library
Board of Trustees meetings. The minutes are the official record of the meeting. There are three
basic types of formats for minutes – action, summary, and verbatim. Action minutes reflect the
action taken, including the maker and second of motions, and the vote of each motion. The
content of presentations and discussions are not included in action minutes. Summary minutes
include the information in action minutes plus a summary of points discussed and individuals’
comments. Verbatim minutes are a “word by word” transcript of the proceedings.

A majority of California cities prepare action minutes. On average, the time to prepare summary
minutes takes 2½ times the length of the meeting. Action minutes streamline the process and
allow for a more efficient use of staff time. It was primarily for this reason that, on April 9, 2014,
the City Council voted to establish the “action” minutes format for itself and all advisory bodies.

On July 27, 2020, the Library Board of Trustees voted to request that the City Council permit
the “summary” format to be utilized for Board meeting minutes. Given the Board’s level of
interaction on Library matters, members felt that a summary of Trustee discussions would be
more helpful in order to track ideas and projects and to better inform future Board members.
On September 9, 2020, the City Council voted to approve of such request.

DISCUSSION

As mentioned above, summary minutes require a significant amount of staff time. In hopes of
better utilizing staff time, Staff is recommending the Board revert back to the “action” format of
minutes. This would align the Library Board of Trustees minutes format with the City Council
and all other City advisory bodies.

 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Board approve of the minutes format change to “action” and request City
Council’s approval.

4. CRAIN ART GALLERY REPORT

Trustee Mollno shared that January and February’s exhibit displayed local watercolor artist, Marie
McDuffie. McDuffie’s theme was local places in San Marino and the surrounding area. Her reception
was cancelled due to the pandemic, but quite a few people still came anyways. The artist sold over
half of her paintings and will be sending over a donation to the Library.
Trustee Mollno shared that there is a little cabinet in the hallway known as the “Trustees’ Cabinet.”
Lynda Lyons of the Crain Art Gallery Committee is in charge of scheduling what goes in the Cabinet.
While McDuffie’s artwork was on display, her sketch book was in the Cabinet to show any non-
artists what a sketch book looks like. In addition to the sketch books, there were also some art
palettes and tools in there, which Trustee Mollno thought were really nice additions to the paintings.
The next exhibit begins on March 9 and will display works by Verdugo Hills Artist Association. It
will be a juried exhibit, which means artists submit paintings and then the juror, Pete Morris from
Los Angeles County, picks the paintings to be included. The title of the exhibit will be Art and
Artistry and there will most likely be no reception.
The following exhibit will display April Drew Foster’s work from April 23 to June 3. Foster had
virtual exhibit in the Gallery during the pandemic, and has been offered an in-person exhibit now
that the Library is open again. There will a reception either at the Library or at her home. The
preferred location for the reception is the Library, since receptions are usually when artists sell
most of their artwork. Director Johnson shared that the Committee can count on that reception
occurring in person at the Library in April.
Trustee Mollno explained that the summer months have not yet been booked with artists. The
September and October exhibit will most likely feature a group called The Plein Airs. One of the
group members, Susan Culter, has already submitted some of the works. The November and
December exhibit will most likely feature Trustee Mollno.
The Crain Art Gallery was established in 2009 as a tribute to former City Librarian, Carolyn Crain,
with restricted donations designated specifically for its formation and maintenance. The Gallery has
its own budget line items. The current Budget Monitor shows a balance of $12,427. Since then, there
has been a donation of $370 from the November/December artist, which will show up on the next
Monitor.

Minutes from the January 2022 meeting, Trustee Mollno thinks that the issue has been resolved. She

BACKGROUND

On June 8, the San Marino Public Library Foundation submitted an Event Permit Application
(Attachment 1) for a fundraiser event occurring on Saturday, October 15, 2022 at the Crowell
Public Library. In conjunction with the application, the Foundation is requesting the closure of
the Library on October 15.

The Foundation has successfully presented Delicious Destinations as a fundraising event to
supplement the needs of the Library. As the Foundation evolves and emerges from the pandemic,
they have decided to offer a new event called Literary Libations to gain community support.

DISCUSSION

The new event, Literary Libations, will offer tastings and libation information from wineries, local
breweries, and a spirits sampling. All of this will be complimented by an array of food tastings by
local caterer, Alexander’s Catering.

The first floor of the Library will be transformed with colorful, literary images ranging from books
to quotes to literary characters. The fundraising elements of the event include ticket sales,
sponsorships, opportunity drawings, a paddle raise, and two separate silent auctions.

Given the event’s size and scope, the Foundation anticipates the decoration preparation to begin
Friday, October 14 after the Library closes and the full following day up to the event. Clean up
and full restoration of the Library is expected by Sunday, October 16 at 1 PM when the Library
is scheduled to reopen.

The purpose of the event is to provide funding for a new Integrated Library System (ILS), which
is the library management system. The ILS can help manage acquisitions (ordering, receiving, and
invoicing materials); cataloging (classifying and indexing materials); circulation (lending materials

as well as online public access catalog or OPAC (public user interface).

  APPENDIX: EVENTS APPLICATION DEFINITIONS AND GUIDELINES

The following Definitions and Guidelines apply to all Special Events and Public Events within the City of San Marino, unless
otherwise specified, and govern the approval and execution of the aforementioned activities.

REMINDER: The City of San Marino may request from the Applicant additional information not listed below deemed
necessary to determine whether the application should be granted, conditionally granted, or denied. A checklist for each
of the following event types can be found on page 2 of this application packet.

SPECIAL PRIVATE EVENTS are events not open to the public and having 100 or more attendees; occurring in an R-
1 Residential Zone; serving a political or charitable nonprofit organization; requiring a fee for entry, collecting donations,
and/or fundraising is taking place.

PUBLIC EVENTS are an assemblage of persons, animals, vehicles, or any combination thereof, that assemble on public
property, including streets, sidewalks, Lacy Park, City Hall, Stoneman School, San Marino Center, Crowell Public Library,
or other areas deemed as property of the City of San Marino. Public Events are categorized into the following:

  •  General Public Events: organized events open to the public that is on or passes through public property or public
  right-of-ways and is comprised of 15+ persons. These are unique from classes or activities that require registration
  and/or a participation fee.
  •  Block Parties: one or more blocks in an R-1 Residential Zone neighborhood are closed for the purpose of a public
  gathering for the persons residing in that neighborhood
  •  Expressive Activities: conduct of which the sole or principal object in the communication of opinions, views, or
  ideas that are protected by the 1st Amendment of the United States Constitution and typically taking place on
  sidewalks and/or the Huntington Drive medians
  •  Spontaneous Events: any public event involving expressive activity that is in response to a public occurrence that
  took place within the last five (5) days

The Community Development Director or their designee reviews the applications for Special Events on Private Property
to determine the issuance of a Special Events Permit. A decision is based on the following criteria:
  1. Compliance with the eligibility criteria
  2. Compliance with the rules in the completed application
  3. The Applicant and persons affiliated are in good standing within one (1) year prior to the date of the proposed
  event being applied for. Good standing will be defined as having complied with all terms and conditions of previous
  event applications executed by the Applicant or affiliated persons and not providing any false information on any
  City applications.

The City Manager or their designee reviews the applications for Events on Public Property to determine the issuance of a
Public Events Permit. A decision is based on the following criteria and in consultation with City Attorney:
  1. Compliance with the eligibility criteria
  2. Availability of the subject public property
  3. Compliance with the rules in the completed application
  4. The Applicant and persons affiliated are in good standing within one (1) year prior to the date of the proposed
  event being applied for. Good standing will be defined as having complied with all terms and conditions of
  previous event applications executed by the Applicant or affiliated persons and not providing any false
  information on any City applications.

A. APPLICATION SUBMITTAL

Event applications must be submitted in accordance to the deadlines outlined in this application, depending on the type of
event permit being sought.

that the Applicant provided all the necessary materials and information (SMMC §16.08.05.G) to ensure they are able to
complete a thorough review of the event request. All applications must be completed via the fillable PDF provided.
Handwritten applications will not be accepted. After an application is submitted, the Community Services Department will
route the application and attachments to the appropriate City Departments and Divisions. An application will be denied,
approved, or conditionally approved by the City in accordance with the deadlines outlined in the table below.

B. APPLICATION REVIEW AND DETERMINATION

Staff may only approve events that are operated in compliance with the San Marino Municipal Code. Staff may impose
conditions of approval for the operations of the temporary use, and may affect the following:
  • Event time period
  • Event duration / hours
  • Date of the event
  • Noise levels
  • Location of temporary structures
  • Waste collection

  • On-site police / security and safety measures

Police Department for policing the proposed event. The Applicant will receive a written determination from City staff that
describes the terms of the approval or denial.

C. APPLICABLE FEES

Fees that are applicable to the submittal of a special event or public event permit are set by the City Council in the Fee
Schedule at the approval of each annual budget. Applicants are required to pay the appropriate fees for submitting this
application. Additional fees may be assessed, as allowed under the policy

D. INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE

The Applicant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its officers, employees, and agents from any and all
losses, costs , expenses, claims, liabilities, actions, or damages, including liability for injuries to any person or persons or
damage to property arising at any time during and/or arising out of or in an way connected with the Applicant’s use or
occupancy of the private or public property, unless solely caused by the gross negligence or willful misconduct of the City,
its officers, employees, or agents.

As a condition precedent to the issuance of a special event or public event permit, the Applicant shall obtain public liability
insurance from an insurance company licensed to do business in the State of California and having a financial rating in
Best’s Insurance Guide of at least “B”. Such insurance shall provide occurrence coverage against liabilities for death,
personal injury, or property damage arising out of or in any way connected with such special event. Such insurance shall
be in the amount of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), combined single limit, and shall name the City and the City’s
officers, employees and agents as additional insureds under the coverage afforded. In addition, such insurance shall be
primary and noncontributing with respect to any other insurance available to the City and shall include a severability of
interest (cross liability) clause. Proof of such insurance, in a form approved by the Director, shall be maintained in full
force and effect throughout the course of the special event authorized by such permit.

representative of the Applicant, which authorizes the organizer to apply for the event permit, is required.

F. SITE PLAN / ROUTE MAP

The Applicant must submit a site plan that draws out the layout of the proposed event. This is applicable for moving routes
and fixed venues. Based on the event site plan and components, the Fire Department and/or Community Development
Department may require an inspection of the venue at the Applicant’s expense before or during the event. The site plan
must include all elements of the event, including but not limited to the following:
  • Chairs
  • Tables
  • Portable structures
  • Stages
  • Bleachers
  • Tents (Note: any tent larger than 250 square feet requires a separate permit)
  • Booths
  • Bars

  the direction of travel is the event is moving or along a route
  • Streets and/or intersections that require soft or hard closures. A traffic control plan will coincide with this item.
  • Location of fencing, barriers, and/or barricades. Indicate any removable fencing for emergency access
  • The provision for a minimum of twenty (20) foot emergency access lanes throughout the event venue
  • Location of first aid facilities and ambulances
  • Location of all stages, platforms, scaffolding, bleachers, grandstands, canopies, tents, portable restrooms, booths,
  beer gardens, cooking arenas, trash containers, dumpsters, and other temporary structures
  • Detail of food booths and cooking area configurations
  • Generator locations and electricity sources
  • Locations and sources of open flames, fuel, and other hazardous material containers
  • Placement of vehicles and/or trailers
  • Exit locations for outdoor events that are fenced or within tents or tent structures
  • Identification of all event components that meet accessibility standards
  • Parking and shuttle plan
  • Other related components not listed above

 G. SECURITY AND TRAFFIC CONTROL

A security plan must be developed that will comply with any conditions established by the San Marino Police
Department. Upon review, the Applicant may be required to enter into a police service contract to hire Police
Department personnel and/or staff for purposes of traffic control and/or crowd control.

A traffic control plan must be completed by a licensed traffic control company (C-31). The plan must also include an
applicable parking plan to show the number of parking stalls that will be available for event staffers, volunteers, and event
participants. If off-site parking is proposed at a different area, the Applicant must include a separate site plan for that
area. If on-street parking or parking restrictions are proposed, the Applicant must provide a diagram showing the
requested restrictions. A detailed narrative should supplement the traffic control plan.

H. CITY CO-SPONSORSHIP

Co-sponsorship by the City of San Marino is approved or denied by the City Council. The Applicant must describe any
in-kind services they are requesting from the City of San Marino. These services include the following:
  • City staff time
  • Permit fees
  • Event promotion using City media services
  • Facility rentals

Furthermore, the Applicant must outline if they are requesting permission to use the City of San Marino logo for event
marketing purposes. Please note that for City co-sponsorship requests, a minimum of ninety (90) days advance notice is
needed to allow for City Council action.

I.  EVENT MARKETING AND NOTIFICATION

The Applicant must describe how they intend on informing the public of their event. This requirement is to ensure
compliance with §16.08.14 of the San Marino Municipal Code whereby it is unlawful to use the City’s name without
authorization.

The description may be brief and concise, but the description must include the date they intend to start publicity. It is
strongly suggested that publicity not start until the Applicant secures the event permit. Furthermore, if the Applicant is
required to notify the community, they must provide a copy of the notice a minimum of three (3) weeks prior to the
event. The notice must be submitted to the Community Services Department for review. Once approved, the notices
must be distributed at least two (2) weeks prior to the event date. Notification area will be determined once the application
is reviewed by applicable City staff.

All temporary signage, on-site and off-site, must also be described in the Application. Off-site signs include signs located

8. REQUEST TO CHANGE THE FORMAT OF THE MINUTES

Management Analyst Shigenaga presented the staff report. She explained that the Library Board is
the only board / commission that utilizes “summary” minutes; all others utilize “action” minutes. She
shared that “summary” minutes require a significantly greater amount of staff time to prepare, so
staff are proposing a change to “action” minutes in hopes of better utilizing staff time.

Trustee Sadun asked if the City has software to transcribe the recording of the minutes. Management
Analyst Shigenaga responded that the City does not have software and that she is the one who
currently prepares the minutes. Director Johnson added that preparing the minutes can take 6-8
hours depending on the length of the meeting. Trustee Sadun asked if the recordings of the meeting
will be available for reference if needed. City Clerk Baker explained that the video and audio
recordings are required to be kept for one year, but are normally kept longer than that. Trustee
Osegueda asked why the Library Board prepares “summary” minutes. Chairperson Domier
explained that a few Board Members had requested more details, so the transition to “summary”
minutes occurred. Trustee Sadun shared that she thinks the Board should try “action” minutes,
especially given the staffing issues, and revisit this again if needed. Alternate Wu and Alternate Wahl
agreed that the Board should try “action” minutes knowing the time demand “summary” minutes
require.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None
